papers_read.title_as_printed: Early MCI-to-AD Conversion Prediction Using Future Value Forecasting of Multimodal Features (Minhas et al., Comput Intell Neurosci 2021)
A Graph Gaussian Embedding Method for Predicting Alzheimer's Disease Progression with MEG Brain Networks (Xu et al., IEEE Trans Biomed Eng 2021)

Transfer learning for predicting conversion from mild cognitive impairment to dementia of Alzheimer's type based on a three-dimensional convolutional neural network (Bae et al., Neurobiol Aging 2021) - read because it is the paper whose figures the P-174 claim quotes

what_each_reports.P-186: SVM on longitudinal 3-visit trajectories (last visit forecast) of 8 neuropsychological measures + FreeSurfer MRI features; ADNI-1 MCI with complete follow-up, 5-fold CV. 1-year-ahead AUC 95.7% (n=85); 6-month-ahead AUC 91.2% (n=119).
what_each_reports.P-174: The PDF supplied for P-174 is the MEG MG2G paper (Madrid cohort, 76 MCI: 28 pMCI/48 sMCI, 53 NC): mean accuracy across 10 classifiers 78% sMCI vs pMCI, 5-fold CV; AUCs only in supplementary figures. It reports no AUC 0.827. The claim's 'AUC 0.827' is Bae et al. (P-37's paper; P-174's summary block is a stub duplicate of P-171, which describes Bae et al.): baseline single-timepoint sMRI ResNet29 3D-CNN with NC-vs-DAT transfer learning, ADNI MCI converters within 3 years (228) vs non-converters stable >=3 years (222), 70/15/15 split, test accuracy 82.4%, AUC 0.827 (68 test scans).

quantity_a: AUC for MCI progressors (conversion by month 36) vs stables in a complete-follow-up ADNI-1 subsample (n=85), input = longitudinal NM+MRI-feature trajectories including a forecast value at the conversion time point, 5-fold CV.
quantity_b: As quoted (Bae et al.): test-set AUC for MCI converting within 3 years vs MCI stable for at least 3 years, input = one baseline raw 3D T1 MRI scan, independent held-out test set of 68 scans. As in the supplied PDF (Xu et al.): mean classification accuracy from MEG alpha-band network embeddings in a Madrid clinic cohort.
incompatible_if_same: No. Neither study reports an AUC interval; with 68 test scans for 0.827 and 85 CV subjects for 0.957, intervals would likely be wide. Neither paper claims an ordering the other refutes.

gates.task: match: T2 conversion prediction in both P-186 and Bae et al. (and the MEG paper's sMCI/pMCI task)
gates.dataset_family: match for Bae et al. (ADNI); mismatch for the supplied P-174 PDF (Hospital Universitario San Carlos, Madrid)
gates.validation_tier: match: internal validation in all (CV or random held-out split)
gates.modality_family: mismatch: P-186 cognitive tests + tabular FreeSurfer features vs Bae et al. raw structural MRI images only (vs MEG in the supplied PDF); no waiver on record

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible: same metric type (AUC) only for the Bae et al. reading, but the input representation differs (longitudinal cognitive + MRI-feature trajectories with a forecast conversion-time value vs a single baseline image), and the population differs (complete-follow-up ADNI-1 subsample vs ADNI MCI with >=3-year stable non-converters). The supplied PDF reports accuracy, not AUC.
performance_validity: flag does not apply: 0.957 and 0.827 are both below 0.97
independence: Bae et al. and P-186 are distinct author groups sharing ADNI (possible subject overlap). The MEG paper shares no cohort. Note P-174 is itself a stub duplicate and P-171 is marked duplicate of P-37, so the claim's source is P-37.
grounds: The PDF for P-174 is the MEG paper, which reports no AUC 0.827; the claim's figure belongs to Bae et al. (the P-37 PDF), so the record is misattached.

Read against Bae et al., the AUC 0.827 comes from a single baseline raw MRI image, while P-186's 0.957 comes from longitudinal cognitive-plus-MRI-feature trajectories including a forecast value at the conversion time point, so input representation and modality differ.
Read against the supplied MEG paper instead, the dataset (Madrid clinic cohort), modality (MEG) and metric (accuracy) all differ from P-186, so the result is incommensurable under either reading.

evidence_quotes.quote: The method proposed in this paper has recorded the highest classification AUC of 95.7% predominantly because of involving the forecasted marker value at the time of conversion as a classification feature.
for 1-year-ahead prediction, the dataset contains three consecutive annual readings, resulting in 35 MCIp and 50 MCIs subjects.
MEG data for this study was collected from 76 MCI patients and 53 age-matched neurotypical controls (NC)
MG2G achieved high performance with 61% for NC/sMCI/pMCI classification, 79% for NC/sMCI classification, 78% for sMCI/pMCI classification, and 82% for NC/pMCI classification.
It produced a test set classification accuracy of 82.4% and 0.827 area under the curve as well as 0.189 equal error rate value (Fig. 4B).
Included in the target task is the single time point sMRI scan at which an individual first received a diagnosis of MCI.

record_defects: claim_b attributes 'AUC 0.827' to P-174, but P-174's PDF (Xu et al., MEG) does not report it; the figure is from Bae et al. (P-37). P-174's summary block is a [STUB-DEDUP-OF-P-171] that 'must not be cited as evidence', and P-171 is itself marked duplicate of P-37.
The index registry row for P-174 describes a 3D-CNN transfer-learning study on ADNI (n=450), which is Bae et al., not the PDF mapped to P-174.
resolution_note says 'Confirmed genuine' on metric type and gap alone while resolution says 'Rejected: Task, dataset, or modality mismatch'.
The long bridging-evidence list names no condition separating the two results.
what_would_change_the_verdict: Nothing on these sources: the verdict holds whether the claim is read against the MEG PDF or against Bae et al. Only a same-input, same-population comparison with non-overlapping intervals could make it genuine.
